#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Refuse a commit message that claims RED-proof without a record a reader can re-open.

Enable once per clone with:  git config core.hooksPath .githooks

WHY THIS EXISTS (D0A-R39). `scripts/weaken-driver.py` decided what counted as RED-proven for
two rounds while nothing recorded or gated that authority — the half of "unwired" that was
never actually deferred. Proof publication already HAS a consumer: reviewers and commit
readers granting credit to the phrase. This is that consumer made mechanical.

IT REFUSES; IT DOES NOT WARN. A rule that advises is DEFECT_CLASSES 54 — a required check
disconnected from acceptance — which is the class this whole mechanism exists to close.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO, stated so nobody reads more into a green commit:
  * `--no-verify` bypasses it, and `core.hooksPath` is per-clone opt-in. This gates the
    DEFAULT path, not a determined author. Repository-wide enforcement is CI.
  * It checks that a claim is RE-OPENABLE, not that it is TRUE. Content-addressing prevents
    post-hoc editing of a record, not fabrication of one.

The canonicalisation is IMPORTED from the producer, never reimplemented: a second copy is
exactly DEFECT_CLASSES 55, a producer and consumer agreeing about the property and disagreeing
about the format, with neither side's tests able to see it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import re
import subprocess
import sys

CLAIM = re.compile(r"RED[-_ ]?PROVEN", re.I)
BACKTICKED = re.compile(r"`[^`]*`")
CITATION = re.compile(r"^\s*weaken-record:\s*([0-9a-f]{16})\s*$", re.I | re.M)
RECORD_DIR = "scratch/weaken-records"


def _root() -> pathlib.Path:
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return pathlib.Path(out.stdout.strip())


def _blob(root: pathlib.Path, rel: str) -> bytes | None:
    """The record as the COMMIT will contain it — index first, then HEAD."""
    for ref in (f":{rel}", f"HEAD:{rel}"):
        got = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), "show", ref], capture_output=True)
        if got.returncode == 0:
            return got.stdout
    return None


def main() -> int:
    message = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text()
    lines = message.splitlines()

    # D0A-R41-03: ONLY DISCARD WHAT GIT IS ESTABLISHED TO REMOVE. The previous version cut at
    # any scissors-looking line. Measured: git truncates at scissors ONLY when the message is
    # to be edited — with `-F` or `-m` every cleanup mode, `scissors` included, keeps that text
    # verbatim, so `# RED-proven` below a hand-written scissors line was published and invisible
    # here. The guard that asserted otherwise asserted the hole.
    #
    # In the EDITOR path git writes its own block and then removes everything below it, and the
    # hook does see that text (a `--verbose` diff would otherwise supply claims nobody made).
    # That block is git's verbatim output, not authored prose, so matching it is reading a
    # known producer rather than guessing intent. If git ever changes the wording this hook
    # stops trimming and refuses MORE, which is the safe direction for drift.
    cut = len(lines)
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if (line.startswith("# ---") and ">8" in line
                and i + 1 < len(lines)
                and lines[i + 1].startswith("# Do not modify or remove the line above")):
            cut = i
            break
    lines = lines[:cut]

    # D0A-R41-03 (second half): AN EXPLICIT FORMAT, rather than a regex pretending to
    # understand assertions. A BACKTICKED token is a narrative reference — naming the constant,
    # quoting a historical verdict — and asks for no credit. An unbackticked one asserts proof
    # and must cite a record. Fail closed WITHIN that format; the format itself is a convention
    # the author controls, which is what stopped a correct commit message needing awkward prose.
    claim_text = BACKTICKED.sub(" ", "\n".join(lines))
    citable = "\n".join(l for l in lines if not l.startswith("#"))
    cited = [m.group(1).lower() for m in CITATION.finditer(citable)]
    claims = bool(CLAIM.search(re.sub(CITATION, "", claim_text)))

    if not claims and not cited:
        return 0

    root = _root()
    wd_path = root / "scripts" / "weaken-driver.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("wd", wd_path)
    wd = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(wd)

    problems: list[str] = []
    if claims and not cited:
        problems.append(
            "this message claims RED-proof but cites no record.\n"
            "    A reader cannot re-open the experiment from prose. Run the weaken through\n"
            "    scripts/weaken-driver.py, stage the record it writes under\n"
            f"    {RECORD_DIR}/, and add a trailer:\n"
            "        weaken-record: <16-hex id>\n"
            "    If the mention is NARRATIVE — naming the constant, quoting a past verdict —\n"
            "    wrap it in backticks: a backticked token asks for no proof credit.")

    for rid in cited:
        rel = f"{RECORD_DIR}/{rid}.json"
        raw = _blob(root, rel)
        if raw is None:
            problems.append(
                f"record {rid} is cited but {rel} is neither staged nor committed.\n"
                "    A citation that does not resolve is the prose it was meant to replace.\n"
                f"    `git add {rel}` so the record lands in this commit.")
            continue
        try:
            rec = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            problems.append(f"record {rid} is not readable JSON: {e}")
            continue
        recomputed = wd.record_id(rec)
        if recomputed != rec.get("id") or recomputed != rid:
            problems.append(
                f"record {rid} does not hash to its own contents "
                f"(stored id {rec.get('id')!r}, recomputed {recomputed!r}).\n"
                "    The record was edited after it was written, or was not written by the\n"
                "    driver. Re-run the weaken; do not repair the file by hand.")
            continue
        if rec.get("verdict") != "RED_PROVEN":
            problems.append(
                f"record {rid} is cited for a RED-proof claim but its verdict is "
                f"{rec.get('verdict')!r}.\n"
                "    That verdict is a statement about the EXPERIMENT, not a weakness in the\n"
                "    target. Cite it for what it says, or re-run the weaken.")
            continue
        # D0A-R40-01: THE EVIDENCE CONTRACT. Checking the hash and the declared verdict
        # accepted `{"id": ..., "verdict": "RED_PROVEN"}` — a record with no experiment in it.
        # The contract lives in the producer and is imported, never restated here.
        failures = wd.validate_record(rec)
        if failures:
            listed = "\n".join(f"      - {f}" for f in failures[:8])
            problems.append(
                f"record {rid} does not satisfy the evidence contract:\n{listed}\n"
                "    A verdict without the observations that produced it is the prose this\n"
                "    trailer exists to replace. Re-run the weaken with a current driver.")

    if not problems:
        return 0
    print("\ncommit-msg REFUSED — a RED-proof claim must be re-openable:\n", file=sys.stderr)
    for p in problems:
        print(f"  * {p}\n", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  (--no-verify bypasses this; it does not make the claim checkable.)\n",
          file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# RED proofs for .githooks/commit-msg — the consumer that gates RED-proof claims.
#
# TIER 1 by §6 clause (d): this hook's acceptance is the evidence that a commit's RED-proof
# claim is re-openable. If it accepts what it should refuse, the claim travels uncheckable,
# which is the state D0A-R39 was opened to end.
#
# The subject is the REAL hook, reached through a SYMLINK into a fake repo (DEFECT_CLASSES
# 25 — a copy would be a different artifact), and so is the real producer, because the hook
# IMPORTS its canonicalisation rather than reimplementing it.

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
REPO=$PWD
work=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
pass=0; fail=0

# D0A-R40-06: every failure reports its label to the side channel, so this suite can be
# DRIVEN by the driver it guards. Without it the driver sees a red suite with no attribution
# and correctly returns UNVERIFIABLE — a suite that cannot say which guard failed cannot
# participate in the contract it exists to defend.
report() {
  [ -n "${DELPHI_GUARD_FAILURE_REPORT:-}" ] && printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$DELPHI_GUARD_FAILURE_REPORT"
  return 0
}
fail_guard() { echo "  [FAIL] $1"; report "$1"; fail=$((fail+1)); }

check() {  # check <label> <expected: accept|refuse> <msgfile> [substring]
  local label=$1 want=$2 msg=$3 want_text=${4:-}
  local out rc
  out=$(cd "$work/repo" && "$work/repo/.githooks/commit-msg" "$msg" 2>&1); rc=$?
  local got=accept; [ $rc -ne 0 ] && got=refuse
  if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
    echo "$out" | sed 's/^/         /'; fail_guard "$label"; return
  fi
  if [ -n "$want_text" ] && ! grep -qF -- "$want_text" <<<"$out"; then
    echo "         refused, but the reason never named: $want_text"
    echo "$out" | sed 's/^/         /'; fail_guard "$label"; return
  fi
  echo "  [OK ] $label"; pass=$((pass+1))
}

mkdir -p "$work/repo/.githooks" "$work/repo/scripts" "$work/repo/scratch/weaken-records"
ln -s "$REPO/.githooks/commit-msg" "$work/repo/.githooks/commit-msg"
ln -s "$REPO/scripts/weaken-driver.py" "$work/repo/scripts/weaken-driver.py"
( cd "$work/repo" && git init -q && git config user.email t@t && git config user.name t \
    && git add -A && git commit -qm init \
    && git config core.hooksPath .githooks )   # so the REAL-commit cases below run the hook

mint() {  # mint <verdict> <discriminator> -> prints the id, writes+stages the record
  python3 - "$work/repo" "$1" "$2" "$REPO" <<'PY'
import importlib.util, json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
root, verdict, disc = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
REPO = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[4])
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("wd", root / "scripts" / "weaken-driver.py")
wd = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(wd)
# A REAL producer record is the base, so these fixtures satisfy the evidence contract the
# way a real one does. A hand-written stub would only prove the hook accepts stubs.
import glob
src = sorted(glob.glob(str(REPO / "scratch" / "weaken-records" / "*.json")))
real = None
for cand in src:
    b = json.loads(pathlib.Path(cand).read_text())
    if b.get("schema") == wd.SCHEMA and not wd.validate_record(b):
        real = b
        break
assert real is not None, "no contract-satisfying record in the ledger to base fixtures on"
body = json.loads(json.dumps(real))
body.pop("id")
body["verdict"] = verdict
body["execution"]["timeout_s"] = 900 + len(disc)   # the discriminator, contract-neutral
body = {"id": wd.record_id(body), **body}
p = root / "scratch" / "weaken-records" / f"{body['id']}.json"
p.write_text(json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n")
subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), "add", str(p)], check=True)
print(body["id"])
PY
}

echo "== .githooks/commit-msg =="
GOOD=$(mint RED_PROVEN one); NOTCAUGHT=$(mint NOT_CAUGHT two)
# A SECOND, GENUINELY DIFFERENT record. A self-referential hash that works on the first and
# breaks on the next is exactly the shape that ships — and the first version of this file
# minted two IDENTICAL bodies, so "two records" silently cited one record twice.
SECOND=$(mint RED_PROVEN three)
if [ "$GOOD" != "$SECOND" ] && [ -n "$GOOD" ] && [ -n "$SECOND" ]; then
  echo "  [OK ] two distinct records mint distinct ids"; pass=$((pass+1))
else
  fail_guard "two distinct records mint distinct ids"
fi

printf 'chore: ordinary commit with no claim\n' > "$work/plain"
check "a message with no claim and no citation is untouched" accept "$work/plain"

printf 'fix: something\n\nThis is RED-proven.\n' > "$work/claim-no-cite"
check "a RED-proof claim with no record is REFUSED" refuse "$work/claim-no-cite" \
  "cites no record"

printf 'fix: x\n\nRED-proven.\n\nweaken-record: 0123456789abcdef\n' > "$work/unresolved"
check "a citation that does not resolve is REFUSED" refuse "$work/unresolved" \
  "neither staged nor committed"

printf 'fix: x\n\nRED-proven.\n\nweaken-record: %s\n' "$NOTCAUGHT" > "$work/wrong-verdict"
check "a record whose verdict is not RED_PROVEN is REFUSED" refuse "$work/wrong-verdict" \
  "its verdict is 'NOT_CAUGHT'"

printf 'fix: x\n\nRED-proven.\n\nweaken-record: %s\n' "$GOOD" > "$work/ok"
check "a claim citing a resolvable RED_PROVEN record is accepted" accept "$work/ok"

printf 'fix: x\n\nRED-proven.\n\nweaken-record: %s\nweaken-record: %s\n' "$GOOD" "$SECOND" \
  > "$work/ok2"
check "...and so is a message citing TWO records" accept "$work/ok2"

# ── D0A-R40-05 / D0A-R41-04: THE REFUSAL-KIND x CITATION-POSITION MATRIX ────────────────
#
# PROVENANCE, because the discipline's whole value is in it and it is invisible afterwards:
#
#   * the KINDS come from D0A-R41-04's own wording — it names "missing, wrong-verdict,
#     corrupted-hash, and contract-invalid" as covered and "unreadable JSON" as omitted.
#     Five. Read from the FINDING, never from the hook, because a matrix derived from the
#     implementation reproduces the implementation's omissions;
#   * the POSITIONS come from the loop's STRUCTURE — `for rid in cited` has a first
#     iteration and a subsequent one, and `cited[:1]` passing proved the second was never
#     load-bearing. Two.
#
# Taking the kinds from the code is what produced the first gap. Taking the positions from
# the finding would have been impossible: it does not know the loop's shape.
mint_bad() {  # mint_bad <kind> -> prints an id that the hook must refuse
  case "$1" in
    missing)   echo "0123456789abcdef" ;;                       # never staged
    wrong-verdict) mint NOT_CAUGHT "wv-$2" ;;
    corrupted)
      local rid; rid=$(mint RED_PROVEN "cor-$2")
      python3 - "$work/repo" "$rid" <<'PY2'
import json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
root, rid = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
p = root / "scratch" / "weaken-records" / f"{rid}.json"
b = json.loads(p.read_text()); b["execution"]["timeout_s"] = 4242   # bytes move, filename does not
p.write_text(json.dumps(b, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n")
subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), "add", str(p)], check=True)
PY2
      echo "$rid" ;;
    contract-invalid)
      python3 - "$work/repo" "$2" <<'PY2'
import importlib.util, json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("wd", root / "scripts" / "weaken-driver.py")
wd = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(wd)
body = {"verdict": "RED_PROVEN", "note": sys.argv[2]}
body = {"id": wd.record_id(body), **body}
p = root / "scratch" / "weaken-records" / f"{body['id']}.json"
p.write_text(json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n")
subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), "add", str(p)], check=True)
print(body["id"])
PY2
      ;;
    unreadable)
      # Exactly 16 hex: a shorter id is not even a CITATION, so the hook would never look
      # at the file and the case would prove nothing. The first draft used 14 and both
      # positions "failed" for that reason instead of the intended one.
      local rid; rid=$(printf 'deadbeef%08x' "$3")
      printf 'this is not JSON at all\n' > "$work/repo/scratch/weaken-records/$rid.json"
      ( cd "$work/repo" && git add "scratch/weaken-records/$rid.json" )
      echo "$rid" ;;
  esac
}

expected_for() {
  case "$1" in
    missing)          echo "neither staged nor committed" ;;
    wrong-verdict)    echo "its verdict is" ;;
    corrupted)        echo "does not hash to its own contents" ;;
    contract-invalid) echo "does not satisfy the evidence contract" ;;
    unreadable)       echo "is not readable JSON" ;;
  esac
}

n=0
for kind in missing wrong-verdict corrupted contract-invalid unreadable; do
  n=$((n+1))
  want=$(expected_for "$kind")
  bad_first=$(mint_bad "$kind" "a$n" "$((n * 2))")
  printf 'fix: x\n\nRED-proven.\n\nweaken-record: %s\nweaken-record: %s\n' \
    "$bad_first" "$GOOD" > "$work/m-$kind-1"
  check "matrix: $kind in the FIRST citation is REFUSED" refuse "$work/m-$kind-1" "$want"
  bad_second=$(mint_bad "$kind" "b$n" "$((n * 2 + 1))")
  printf 'fix: x\n\nRED-proven.\n\nweaken-record: %s\nweaken-record: %s\n' \
    "$GOOD" "$bad_second" > "$work/m-$kind-2"
  check "matrix: $kind in the SECOND citation is REFUSED" refuse "$work/m-$kind-2" "$want"
done

# ── D0A-R40-04 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Git's `default` cleanup strips `#` lines only when the message is EDITED. With -F or -m it
# publishes them verbatim, so a claim in a comment was published by git and invisible to a
# hook that discarded every `#` line. Verified against REAL commits below, not just the hook.
printf 'chore: probe\n# RED-proven with no record\n' > "$work/hash-claim"
check "a claim in a COMMENT line is still a claim" refuse "$work/hash-claim" "cites no record"

# ...and the converse fails closed too: a citation git might strip cannot discharge a claim.
printf 'fix: x\n\nRED-proven.\n# weaken-record: %s\n' "$GOOD" > "$work/hash-cite"
check "a citation in a COMMENT line does NOT discharge a claim" refuse "$work/hash-cite" \
  "cites no record"

# ── D0A-R41-03 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# THE GUARD THAT USED TO SIT HERE ASSERTED THE HOLE. It claimed text below any scissors-looking
# line supplies no claim, and git keeps that text verbatim under -F in EVERY cleanup mode,
# `scissors` included — truncation happens only when the message is EDITED. So the R40-04 fix
# for a cleanup mismatch encoded a new cleanup mismatch as an invariant, which is worse than
# leaving it untested: a wrong guard defends the defect against the next person who notices.
printf 'chore: probe\n\n# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------\nRED-proven with no citation\n' \
  > "$work/author-scissors"
check "a claim below an AUTHOR-written scissors line is REFUSED" refuse \
  "$work/author-scissors" "cites no record"

# ...and git's OWN block, which it writes only in the editor path and then removes, is trimmed
# — otherwise a --verbose diff would supply claims nobody made. The hook sees that text.
printf 'chore: probe\n\n# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------\n# Do not modify or remove the line above.\n# Everything below it will be ignored.\ndiff --git a/x b/x\n+this line mentions RED-proven in a diff\n' \
  > "$work/git-scissors"
check "git's own scissors block is trimmed, so a diff supplies no claim" accept \
  "$work/git-scissors"

# An explicit format beats a regex pretending to understand assertions: a BACKTICKED token is
# a narrative reference and asks for no credit.
printf 'chore: probe\n\nThe record carried `RED_PROVEN` and the other carried `UNVERIFIABLE`.\n' \
  > "$work/backticked"
check "a BACKTICKED token is narrative, not an assertion" accept "$work/backticked"
printf 'chore: probe\n\nThis change is RED-proven.\n' > "$work/unbackticked"
check "...and an unbackticked one still asserts and must cite" refuse "$work/unbackticked" \
  "wrap it in backticks"

# REAL commits, because the hook's view and git's stored message must agree.
real_commit() {  # real_commit <file> -> prints "exit=N stored=<yes|no>"
  local rc out
  out=$(cd "$work/repo" && git commit --allow-empty -q -F "$1" 2>&1); rc=$?
  local stored=no
  if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && (cd "$work/repo" && git log -1 --format=%B | grep -q 'RED-proven'); then
    stored=yes
  fi
  echo "exit=$rc stored=$stored"
}
res=$(real_commit "$work/hash-claim")
if [ "$res" = "exit=1 stored=no" ]; then
  echo "  [OK ] a REAL commit with a commented claim is refused, not published"; pass=$((pass+1))
else
  fail_guard "a REAL commit with a commented claim is refused, not published"; echo "         $res"
fi

# Edit the record after the fact. The bytes no longer hash to the id it is filed under.
python3 - "$work/repo" "$GOOD" <<'PY'
import json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
root, rid = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
p = root / "scratch" / "weaken-records" / f"{rid}.json"
b = json.loads(p.read_text()); b["verdict"] = "RED_PROVEN"; b["expectation"]["guard"] = "edited"
p.write_text(json.dumps(b, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n")
subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), "add", str(p)], check=True)
PY
check "a record edited after it was written is REFUSED" refuse "$work/ok" \
  "does not hash to its own contents"

echo
echo "$pass passed, $fail failed"
[ $fail -eq 0 ]
